description: Raga profiles for the Vocal Gym kalpana swara generator: swara roles, gamaka, sourced phrases, avoid rules and allied ragas for the 86 engine ragas (72 melakartas + 14 janyas). Built only from the project research notes; where the notes have nothing, arrays are empty and the gap is recorded. Computed fields (directionRuleOk, inEngineRange, anyaSwaras, features, confidence.phrases) are checked against the engine by test/raga-profiles.test.js and scripts/check-raga-profiles.js. Companion documentation: docs/raga-profiles.md.

notation.letters: S R G M P D N stand for the raga's own swarasthanas (Mohanam G = G3; Hindolam D = D1; Kambhoji N = N2). Pitches are semitones above Sa, as in the engine (S = 0, tara S = 12).
notation.octave: A trailing apostrophe marks tara (S' = 12, R' in Kalyani = 14); a trailing dot marks mandra (N. in Kalyani = -1).
notation.karvai: "," is a karvai (held or silent unit). It is ignored for pitch and for the direction check.
notation.tokens: Tokens are separated by single spaces. Source notation is kept in phrase notes where it matters.
notation.anyaSwara: An explicit variant such as N2 (Bilahari), N3. (Kambhoji) or D1 (old Abheri) names a swara outside the engine scale. Such phrases list it in anyaSwaras and have directionRuleOk = false.
notation.scale: scale.arohana and scale.avarohana are written from the engine (variant numbers for every swara) and must equal it.

generatorGuidance.overview: Use the profile to bias kalpana() among moves it already allows. The feasibility tables stay in charge: nothing here may make an illegal or unfinishable round possible. Phrases become extra devices; landing and avoid data adjust the familiarity score F; janta/dattu tags scale the existing janta and dattu devices.
generatorGuidance.phrases: Treat each phrase with directionRuleOk = true and inEngineRange = true as an extra conventional device (kind conv) whose notes are the phrase pitches and whose durations are 1 per swara plus 1 per following karvai. Offer it only where the reach table says the round can still finish after it, and where the step from the current swara into its first swara is legal (or equal). Add weight x typeFactor to F, with typeFactor signature 1.0, ending 0.9 (and only when the phrase ends the body or the round), janta 0.8, dattu 0.8, connective 0.6. Scale by confidence.phrases: high 1.0, medium 0.8, low 0.5. Do not add phrases to N (novelty); they are the conventional pole.
generatorGuidance.weights: weight = base(source reliability: high 0.8, medium 0.6, low 0.25) x 0.8 if octaveCertain is false, + 0.1 for signature phrases, capped by context (hindustani-reference 0.15, dikshitar-school 0.1, historical-lakshana 0.3). Explicit overrides are explained in the phrase note (e.g. disputed raga identity of the source composition, garbled extraction, possible transcription artefact).
generatorGuidance.octaves: Use phrases at their written octave. Where octaveCertain is false the octave was inferred by the researcher; a generator may also try the phrase one octave up or down if the shifted phrase stays inside the kalpana range (mandra P to tara P).
generatorGuidance.directionRule: Phrases with directionRuleOk = false (anya swaras or a step against the arohana/avarohana) are documented exceptions. Never split them into steps and never let the sampler wander into them note by note. If used at all, emit the whole phrase atomically, check legality only at its entry and exit, and keep them behind a flag (off by default) until a teacher confirms them.
generatorGuidance.landing: kalpanaHints.landingSwaras replaces the engine's generic "held last swara on Sa or Pa" bonus: give +0.6 F to a held swara (dur 2, the cad device, the mora phrase's last swara, the body's last swara) that is in landingSwaras, and a -0.4 F penalty to holds on avoidLanding swaras. swaraRoles.nyasa is the sourced subset; basis says whether the list is sourced, inferred from composition line endings, mixed, or the S/P default. The eduppu target is still chosen by the user; landing data only shapes where the body rests on the way.
generatorGuidance.avoid: avoid entries with swaras: strength hard means remove any candidate device whose notes contain that subsequence (apply inside the device-application table so feasibility stays exact); strength soft means -1.0 F when the candidate creates it. avoid entries with a rule (no swaras) are guidance for future duration/gamaka-aware scoring; the current engine can approximate "do not hold X" by treating X like an avoidLanding swara.
generatorGuidance.jantaDattu: janta and dattu fields scale the F of the engine's janta/janta3/skipjanta and dattu devices: suits x1.3, neutral x1.0, unknown x1.0, avoid x0.5. "unknown" means no evidence either way, not a prohibition.
generatorGuidance.contexts: context carnatic is the default. hindustani-reference phrases describe the Hindustani form of a borrowed raga; dikshitar-school phrases belong to the asampurna raganga, not the sampurna mela the engine uses; historical-lakshana phrases document older forms. They are capped at low weights and are best kept for a "historical colour" option.
generatorGuidance.fallback: When phrases is empty (confidence.phrases none) or all phrases are filtered out, fall back to the generic devices with landingSwaras (S and P by default). For melakartas with vivadiPairs, the notes suggest (as an unsourced design heuristic) lower weight for janta or direct oscillation inside a vivadi pair (e.g. R1 G1 R1 G1) and higher weight for passing through it in one sweep, with S, P and M as the safest landings.
generatorGuidance.gamaka: gamaka texts are descriptive. The engine has no gamaka model yet; use them for tutor display and, later, for rendering or for the conformance scorer.
generatorGuidance.allied: allied lists confusable ragas and how they differ. Entries with basis structural are the mela twin with the other madhyama; all others are sourced. Use them to explain feedback and to design avoid rules; they are not enforced automatically.

melakartaNotes.vivadiPairs: vivadiPairs lists the clashing pairs present in a melakarta: R1-G1 (G1 sounds at the R2 pitch), R3-G3 (R3 at the G2 pitch), D1-N1 (N1 at the D2 pitch) and D3-N3 (D3 at the N2 pitch). 40 of the 72 melas have vivadi swaras; "vivadi dosha" is said to be overcome by singing the vivadi swaras in certain phrases, but no source reached gives performer rules for them.
melakartaNotes.dikshitarSchool: dikshitarName is the asampurna-paddhati (Dikshitar school) counterpart. Most counterparts use the same swaras with vakra or varja rules chosen to avoid direct vivadi runs, so their phrases are not drop-in material for the straight sampurna melas the engine uses. Exceptions with the same straight scale: Jaganmohinam (38), Dhalivarali (39), Girvani (43), Shivapantuvarali (45).
melakartaNotes.koteeswaraIyer: Koteeswara Iyer composed one kriti in each of the 72 melas (Kanda Ganamudam) to show that the vivadi ragas can be performed; their notations are the best future source of idiomatic sampurna phrases for the rare melas. Only "Antaranga bhakti" (Shadvidamargini) was found online.

kambhoji.name: Kambhoji

scale.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S'
scale.avarohana: S' N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S

scaleNotes: Darbar's avarohana ends "S N3. P. D. S": kakali N3 is an anya swara in that mandra phrase, which makes the scale vakra ("shadava-vakra sampurna"). The engine omits N3.

Arohana dispute: the SSP-attested Kambhoji uses "S R M G P D S'" (guruguha prefers SRMGP); linear "S R G M P" is "common in modern Kambhoji" but closer to Harikambhoji. The engine keeps the linear arohana.

N3 dispute: darbar presents it as defining; Prof. S. R. Janakiraman hears the kakali shade as "virtually nil or very alpa", arising from a glide from tara S to P. Archaic Kambhoji used only kaishiki N (S185).

swaraRoles.note: No jiva swara labelled. Vadi-samvadi S-M, S-P, R-D, R-P, G-D.

gamaka.D: Swings widely in the P-D-S context (distinguishes it from Harikambhoji and Khamas).
gamaka.N: Cannot be used to ascend; the N3 shade is a passing colour in a S'-to-P glide, not a held note.

N.interpretation: "a passing colour in a S'-to-P glide, not a held note".
